title: Hoeffding tail bound for a sum of bounded independent variables
hypotheses_covered: t random variables Y_i, with t ≥ 1
each Y_i is almost everywhere measurable
each Y_i almost surely lies in [0,1]
replaced:
Let $(\Omega', \mu)$ be a probability space and let $Y_0, \dots, Y_{t-1} : \Omega' \to
\mathbb{R}$ be mutually independent, a.e.\ $[0,1]$-valued random variables satisfying
$\mathbb{E}[Y_i] \le \varepsilon$ for all $i$, with $\varepsilon \ge 0$ and $c > 1$.
Then
\[
  \mu\!\left\{\omega \;\middle|\; c\,\varepsilon\,t \le \sum_{i=0}^{t-1} Y_i(\omega)\right\}
  \;\le\;
  \exp\!\left(-2(c-1)^2\varepsilon^2 t\right).
\]
